questions.question: Which state in India has the highest population density as per the 2011 census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihar has the **highest population density** among all Indian states as per the 2011 Census, with a density of **1,106 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• It is followed by West Bengal (1,028 persons per square kilometer) and Kerala (860 persons per square kilometer).
 
• The population density is calculated as the **number of people living per unit area of land**, typically per square kilometer.
 
• Bihar's high population density is attributed to factors like **limited land area**, high fertility rates, and a large rural population dependent on agriculture.
 
• Despite its high population density, Bihar's per capita income remains **lower than the national average**, indicating socio-economic challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density:** It is a key demographic metric used to measure the concentration of population in a specific geographic area. High density often results in resource constraints.
 
• **2011 Census of India:** The 2011 Census is the 15th Census conducted in India, providing data on population size, density, literacy rates, and other socio-economic indicators.
 
• **Low Density States:** Arunachal Pradesh has the **lowest population density** among Indian states, with only 17 persons per square kilometer as per the 2011 Census.
 
• **Urbanization Impact:** High population density is typically associated with urban areas, but in Bihar, it is seen even in rural regions due to its agrarian economy and limited industrialization.
 
• **Future Trends:** Population density is expected to increase in states like Bihar, making it crucial to address challenges in infrastructure, healthcare, and education to ensure sustainable development.

questions.question: Who among the following started the Khilafat Movement against the British government?

options.text: Syed Raza Ali and Muhammad Ali Jinnah
Maulana Mazharul Haque and Mian Abdul Aziz

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Khilafat Movement was launched in 1919 by **Shaukat Ali** and **Mohammad Ali**, popularly known as the Ali Brothers, to protest against the British government.
 
• The movement aimed to restore the position of the Ottoman Caliph, who was considered the spiritual leader of the Muslims worldwide.
 
• This movement was a significant part of India's freedom struggle, as it united Hindus and Muslims in a common cause against the British.
 
• It was closely linked to the Non-Cooperation Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, fostering Hindu-Muslim unity during that period.
 
• The movement lost momentum after the abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in Turkey in 1924.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background of the Khilafat Movement:**

 
 
• The Ottoman Empire, led by the Caliph, was dismembered after World War I, and the Treaty of Sèvres (1920) further weakened the Caliph's position.
 
• Indian Muslims viewed the weakening of the Caliphate as a threat to their religious identity and sought to defend it.
 
 
 
• **Ali Brothers:**
 
 
• Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali were key leaders of the Khilafat Movement, actively organizing protests and rallies.
 
• Their leadership was instrumental in mobilizing the Muslim community across India.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**
 
 
• The Khilafat Movement merged with the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi, creating a broader base for anti-British sentiment.
 
• Both movements emphasized non-violent resistance against British policies.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Movement:**
 
 
• The abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in 1924 marked the end of the Khilafat Movement's primary objective.
 
• Additionally, growing communal tensions in the 1920s weakened Hindu-Muslim unity, leading to the movement's decline.

questions.question: Which of the following country’s official language is Sinhala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sinhala** is one of the two official languages of Sri Lanka, alongside Tamil, as per the Sri Lankan constitution.
 
• Sinhala belongs to the **Indo-Aryan language family**, which is a branch of the Indo-European languages.
 
• Around **16 million people in Sri Lanka** speak Sinhala as their first language, making it the majority language of the country.
 
• The Sinhala script, which is unique, is used for writing Sinhala and has been derived from the ancient Brahmi script.
 
• Sri Lanka is a multi-ethnic and multilingual country, but Sinhala is predominantly spoken by the Sinhalese ethnic group, who make up about **75% of the population**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sinhala Language Origins:**

 
 
• Sinhala evolved from the ancient Indo-Aryan languages introduced to Sri Lanka by migrants from the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It has been influenced by Pali, Sanskrit, and Dravidian languages, especially Tamil.
 
 
 
• **Official Language Policy of Sri Lanka:**
 
 
• The Official Languages Act of 1956 made Sinhala the sole official language, which was later amended to include Tamil in 1987.
 
• English is widely used as a **link language** in government and education.
 
 
 
• **Sinhala Literature:**
 
 
• Sinhala has a rich literary tradition dating back to at least the 9th century CE.
 
• Ancient texts like the **Mahavamsa**, a historical chronicle, were written in Pali but heavily influenced Sinhala literature.
 
 
 
• **Sinhalese Ethnic Group:**
 
 
• The Sinhalese are the largest ethnic group in Sri Lanka, primarily practicing Buddhism.
 
• Their culture, festivals, and traditions are closely tied to the Sinhala language and Buddhist practices.

questions.question: Who among the following Dance Gurus got Padma Vibhushan in the year 2000?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelucharan Mohapatra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra** was a renowned Indian classical dancer and guru, credited with the revival of **Odissi dance**.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian award, in the year **2000**, for his contributions to Indian classical dance.
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra dedicated his life to teaching and performing Odissi, bringing it global recognition as a major classical dance form of India.
 
• He was also a celebrated choreographer, known for blending traditional Odissi with innovative elements, making his performances unique and timeless.
 
• He trained numerous accomplished Odissi dancers, including Sanjukta Panigrahi, who further popularized the dance form both nationally and internationally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi Dance**

 
 
• Odissi is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by its fluid movements, intricate footwork, and sculpturesque poses inspired by temple art.
 
• Odissi traditionally narrates stories from Hindu epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana, often dedicated to Lord Jagannath.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• The Padma Awards—Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri—are among India’s highest civilian honors, recognizing achievements in various fields.
 
• Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award, given for "exceptional and distinguished service."
 
 
 
• **Notable Contributions of Kelucharan Mohapatra**
 
 
• He reconstructed and revived traditional Odissi dance forms that were on the verge of decline in the mid-20th century.
 
• His choreographic works include iconic pieces like "Dashavatara" and "Pallavi."
 
 
 
• **Other Dance Gurus and Padma Awards**
 
 
• **Birju Maharaj**: Renowned Kathak dancer, recipient of Padma Vibhushan in 1986.
 
• **Bipin Singh**: Key figure in the revival of Manipuri dance, although not awarded the Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: Who among the following authors wrote ‘Kamayani’, ‘Dhruvswamini’, ‘Kankal’, ‘Titli’, ‘Skandagupta’, ‘Lahar’ and ‘Mamta’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaishankar Prasad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jaishankar Prasad was a renowned Hindi poet, playwright, and novelist, primarily associated with the Chhayavad (Neo-romanticism) literary movement in Hindi literature.
 
• He authored celebrated works such as **'Kamayani'**, which is considered one of the greatest epic poems in Hindi literature.
 
• His notable dramas include **'Dhruvswamini'** and **'Skandagupta'**, which reflect themes of Indian history and valor.
 
• Other famous literary works by him include novels like **'Kankal'** and **'Titli'**, and collections of stories and poetry like **'Lahar'** and **'Mamta'**.
 
• Jaishankar Prasad's literary contributions played a pivotal role in shaping modern Hindi literature and establishing it as a prominent literary language in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhayavad Movement:**

 
 
• Chhayavad was a Hindi literary movement that emerged in the early 20th century, characterized by romanticism, mysticism, and a focus on emotions and individualism.
 
• Key figures of this movement included Jaishankar Prasad, Suryakant Tripathi Nirala, Mahadevi Verma, and Sumitranandan Pant.
 
 
 
• **'Kamayani':**
 
 
• 'Kamayani' is a philosophical and allegorical epic that explores human emotions like faith, love, and intellect through mythological characters.
 
• The poem is divided into cantos, each representing a different emotion or concept, such as Shraddha (Faith) and Manas (Mind).
 
 
 
• **'Dhruvswamini':**
 
 
• It is a historical drama that portrays the story of a queen who rebels against societal norms for her dignity and love.
 
• The play reflects Prasad's progressive views on women's empowerment and self-determination.
 
 
 
• **Jaishankar Prasad's Legacy:**
 
 
• He was awarded the title of "Prasad" for his literary excellence and remains a foundational figure in Hindi literature.
 
• His works continue to influence contemporary writers and are part of academic curricula in India.

questions.question: There shall be a/an ________ with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President in the exercise of his functions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Council of Ministers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Council of Ministers is headed by the Prime Minister and aids and advises the President in the exercise of his functions, as per Article 74 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It comprises various categories of ministers, including Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
 
• The advice tendered by the Council of Ministers to the President is binding, ensuring the President acts in accordance with democratic principles.
 
• The Prime Minister serves as the link between the President and the Council of Ministers, facilitating effective governance.
 
• Decisions taken by the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, ensuring accountability to the legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 74:** The Indian Constitution mandates that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President.
 
• **Collective Responsibility:** The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, ensuring the government remains accountable to elected representatives.
 
• **Role of Prime Minister:** The Prime Minister acts as the head of the Council of Ministers, coordinating its functions and serving as the chief adviser to the President.
 
• **Binding Advice:** The advice provided by the Council of Ministers is binding on the President, emphasizing the democratic structure of governance.
 
• **Categories of Ministers:** The Council includes Cabinet Ministers (senior-level decision-makers), Ministers of State (junior ministers with independent charges or assisting Cabinet Ministers), and Deputy Ministers (assist in specific portfolios).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Chlorine has the highest electron affinity, while fluorine has the highest electronegativity.
Fluorine has the highest electron affinity, while chlorine has the highest electronegativity.
Fluorine has the highest electron affinity and the highest electronegativity.
Fluorine has the highest electron affinity, while bromine has the highest electronegativity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorine has the highest electron affinity, while fluorine has the highest electronegativity.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chlorine has the highest electron affinity** due to its optimal atomic size, which allows it to efficiently gain an electron and release energy in the process.
 
• **Fluorine has the highest electronegativity** (value of 3.98 on the Pauling scale), as it has a strong tendency to attract shared electrons in a chemical bond due to its small size and high nuclear charge.
 
• Electron affinity refers to the energy released when a neutral atom in the gas phase gains an electron to form a negative ion.
 
• Electronegativity, on the other hand, measures the ability of an atom to attract shared electrons in a chemical bond.
 
• The difference arises because fluorine's small size causes strong electron-electron repulsions, slightly reducing its electron affinity compared to chlorine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electron Affinity:**

 
 
• The trend of electron affinity generally increases across a period and decreases down a group in the periodic table.
 
• Chlorine's electron affinity is approximately 349 kJ/mol, the highest among all elements.
 
• Fluorine's electron affinity is slightly lower at about 328 kJ/mol due to increased electron repulsion in its compact atomic structure.
 
 
 
• **Electronegativity:**
 
 
• Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group, following the periodic trend.
 
• Fluorine, being the most electronegative element, plays a key role in various chemical reactions, including the formation of polar covalent bonds.
 
 
 
• **Electron-Electron Repulsion:**
 
 
• Smaller atoms like fluorine experience higher repulsion among valence electrons, which can slightly reduce the energy released during electron addition.
 
• This is why chlorine, despite being larger, has a higher electron affinity than fluorine.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Chemistry:**
 
 
• Electronegativity is crucial in determining bond polarity and molecular geometry.
 
• Electron affinity values are used to predict the likelihood of an atom forming negative ions in reactions.

questions.question: In which game are terms like break, cannons, cue, potting, and kissed commonly used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Billiards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Billiards is a cue sport played on a rectangular table covered with cloth, typically green, and bounded by cushions.
 
• Terms such as "break," "cannons," "cue," "potting," and "kissed" are integral parts of the game's vocabulary.
 
• The cue is a stick used to strike the cue ball, aiming to pot balls or achieve specific objectives in the game.
 
• "Potting" refers to the act of sending a ball into a pocket, while "kissed" describes unintended contact between balls.
 
• Billiards has various forms, including carom billiards, English billiards, and pocket billiards (pool), each with unique rules and gameplay styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Break:** The initial shot in billiards or pool that scatters the balls.
 
• **Cue:** A wooden or composite stick used to hit the cue ball.
 
• **Cannons:** In English billiards, cannons occur when the cue ball strikes two other balls in succession.
 
• **Pockets:** Recessed areas at the edges of the table where balls are potted.
 
• **History:** Billiards originated in the 15th century and was initially played outdoors before transitioning to indoor tables.
 
• **Professional Play:** Billiards tournaments are held globally, including popular events like the World Snooker Championship and Nine-ball Pool tournaments.

questions.question: Who was sent as an envoy to China during the time of Muhammad bin Tughluq?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibn Battuta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ibn Battuta**, a Moroccan traveler and scholar, was sent as an envoy to China by Muhammad bin Tughluq.
 
• He served as a Qadi (Islamic judge) during his time at Muhammad bin Tughluq's court.
 
• Ibn Battuta's travels in India were part of his larger journey across the Islamic world, which lasted for nearly three decades.
 
• His travels and experiences were documented in his famous work, the **Rihla** (The Journey).
 
• Muhammad bin Tughluq appointed Ibn Battuta for diplomatic missions due to his expertise in Islamic law and his reputation as an accomplished traveler.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq:** He was the Sultan of Delhi from 1325 to 1351 and is known for his ambitious projects and administrative experiments, some of which were ahead of their time.
 
• **Rihla:** The Rihla is Ibn Battuta's travelogue, providing a comprehensive account of his travels across Africa, Asia, and Europe, and is a valuable historical source.
 
• **Envoys in History:** During medieval times, sending envoys was a common practice to establish diplomatic relations, negotiate treaties, and maintain trade networks.
 
• **Role of Qadis:** Qadis were Islamic judges responsible for interpreting and implementing Sharia law, often serving in administrative capacities in Islamic courts.
 
• **Travel in the Islamic World:** Ibn Battuta's journey reflects the interconnectedness of the Islamic world during the 14th century, facilitated by shared religion, trade routes, and cultural exchanges.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the 'UPI Safety Ambassador' by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) to enhance safety awareness on digital payment platforms in November 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pankaj Tripathi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pankaj Tripathi has been appointed as the 'UPI Safety Ambassador' by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in November 2023.
 
• The initiative aims to enhance safety awareness regarding digital payments and the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) ecosystem.
 
• As an ambassador, Pankaj Tripathi will promote safe transaction practices and educate users about fraud prevention methods.
 
• NPCI is focusing on leveraging the popularity and trusted image of the actor to reach a broader audience.
 
• This campaign is part of NPCI's ongoing efforts to ensure secure and reliable digital payments in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unified Payments Interface (UPI):**

 
 
• UPI is a real-time payment system developed by NPCI that facilitates instant money transfers between bank accounts via a mobile platform.
 
• Launched in 2016, it has revolutionized digital transactions in India, enabling seamless payments across businesses and individuals.
 
• UPI supports various services such as QR code payments, bill payments, and peer-to-peer money transfers.
 
• It is supported by major banks and payment platforms, making it one of the most widely used payment systems in India.
 
 
 
• **NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India):**
 
 
• NPCI is an umbrella organization for operating retail payment systems in India, established in 2008.
 
• It is responsible for implementing innovative payment systems like UPI, Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS), and RuPay cards.
 
• NPCI works under the guidance of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Indian Banks' Association (IBA).
 
• The organization aims to promote robust and secure payment infrastructure in India.
 
 
 
• **Digital Payment Safety Tips:**
 
 
• Always use strong passwords and enable two-factor authentication for payment apps.
 
• Verify recipient details before transferring funds to avoid fraudulent transactions.
 
• Avoid sharing sensitive information like PINs or OTPs with anyone.
 
• Regularly update payment apps to benefit from improved security features.
 
 
 
• **Fraud Prevention in UPI:**
 
 
• Be cautious of phishing attempts and fraudulent apps claiming to offer UPI services.
 
• Report suspicious activities or unauthorized transactions to your bank or payment platform immediately.
 
• Educate yourself about common scams such as fake QR codes or fraudulent payment requests.
 
• NPCI has introduced features like transaction limits and real-time alerts to enhance security.

questions.question: Which Indian city hosted the Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy event in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ranchi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, hosted the prestigious Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy in 2023.
 
• The tournament featured top teams from Asia, including India, Japan, China, South Korea, Malaysia, and Thailand.
 
• This event was a significant milestone for Ranchi, which has been emerging as a hub for sports in India.
 
• The Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy is a biennial event organized by the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF).
 
• India's women's hockey team participated with strong performances, reflecting the country's growing prominence in international hockey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asian Hockey Federation (AHF):**

 
 
• The governing body for field hockey in Asia, responsible for organizing tournaments such as the Asian Games and the Champions Trophy.
 
• Founded in 1958, the AHF is affiliated with the International Hockey Federation (FIH).
 
 
 
• **Ranchi's Contribution to Sports:**
 
 
• Ranchi is known for producing notable athletes, including cricket icon Mahendra Singh Dhoni.
 
• The city has hosted several national and international sports events, boosting its sports infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **India's Women's Hockey Team:**
 
 
• The Indian women's hockey team has been making significant strides on the global stage, including their historic 4th place finish at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.
 
• The team is currently ranked among the top 10 in the FIH world rankings.
 
 
 
• **Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy:**
 
 
• The tournament was first held in 2010 and serves as a platform for Asian teams to compete at the highest level.
 
• It fosters regional hockey development and prepares teams for global competitions such as the Hockey World Cup and the Olympics.

questions.question: Who is known to have revived Bharatanatyam dance form in its modern version today?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rukmini Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale** is credited with reviving Bharatanatyam, a classical dance form, from its decline during colonial rule.
 
• She redefined Bharatanatyam by removing its association with temple rituals and presenting it as a respectable art form on stage.
 
• Rukmini Devi introduced innovations such as incorporating themes from Indian mythology and epics into Bharatanatyam performances.
 
• She was the first woman to perform Bharatanatyam on stage in its modern form, breaking societal taboos of the time.
 
• In addition to her contributions to dance, Rukmini Devi was also a theosophist, animal rights activist, and a member of the Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam:** A classical Indian dance form originating from Tamil Nadu that combines expression (abhinaya), melody (raga), rhythm (tala), and spiritual themes.
 
• **Devadasi System:** Historically, Bharatanatyam was performed by temple dancers called Devadasis as part of religious rituals. This practice declined during colonial rule.
 
• **Theosophy and Dance:** Rukmini Devi's involvement in the Theosophical Society influenced her vision of Bharatanatyam as a spiritual and cultural art form.
 
• **Kalakshetra Foundation:** Rukmini Devi founded this institution in Chennai to promote and teach Bharatanatyam and other traditional Indian arts.
 
• **Recognition:** Rukmini Devi received several honors, including the Padma Bhushan (1956), for her contributions to Indian art and culture.

questions.question: Megasthenes was an ambassador who was sent to the court of which Indian ruler by the Greek ruler, Seleucus Nicator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by **Seleucus Nicator** to the court of the Mauryan ruler, **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• He authored the famous historical account **‘Indica’**, which provides valuable insights into the Mauryan Empire and Indian society during that period.
 
• Megasthenes described the administrative system, social structure, economy, and culture of the Mauryan Empire in his works.
 
• The relationship between Seleucus Nicator and Chandragupta was formalized through a treaty, including a matrimonial alliance and territorial concessions to Chandragupta.
 
• Megasthenes’ writings are considered one of the earliest and most significant Greek accounts of ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the **Mauryan Empire** in ancient India (circa 321 BCE).
 
• Chandragupta unified most of the Indian subcontinent under his rule, creating one of the largest empires in Indian history.
 
• Under his reign, the Mauryan Empire established a centralized administrative structure and efficient governance.
 
 
 
• **Seleucus Nicator:**
 
 
• Seleucus I Nicator was a general under Alexander the Great and later established the Seleucid Empire.
 
• He ceded territories in modern-day Afghanistan and Pakistan to Chandragupta in exchange for 500 war elephants, which played a crucial role in his campaigns.
 
 
 
• **Indica by Megasthenes:**
 
 
• The book provides an account of Indian geography, society, religion, and governance.
 
• Although the original text is lost, fragments of it survive through later historians like Strabo, Arrian, and Diodorus.
 
 
 
• **The Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• It was one of the most powerful empires in ancient India and reached its zenith under Chandragupta’s grandson, Ashoka.
 
• The Mauryan administration was known for its efficient governance and detailed bureaucratic systems.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 with the help of MG Ranade?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Servants of India Society was founded by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** in **1905**.
 
• The organization was established with the aim to train Indians to serve their country through dedicated social and political work.
 
• Gokhale, a prominent social reformer and leader, was influenced by his mentor, **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade**.
 
• The society emphasized education, social reform, and national unity to prepare individuals for selfless service to the nation.
 
• It played a significant role in the Indian independence movement by encouraging public service and civic responsibility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**:

 
 
• He was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a moderate reformist.
 
• He is considered one of the political mentors of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He worked for the upliftment of the marginalized and promoted the use of education to achieve social progress.
 
 
 
• **Justice MG Ranade**:
 
 
• He was a social reformer, economist, and judge of the Bombay High Court.
 
• Ranade advocated for social reforms such as widow remarriage and the abolition of child marriage.
 
 
 
• **Other Contributions of the Servants of India Society**:
 
 
• The society established schools, libraries, and cooperative societies across India.
 
• It worked to address issues like caste discrimination, untouchability, and illiteracy.
 
 
 
• **Moderates vs Extremists in Congress**:
 
 
• Gokhale belonged to the moderate faction of the Indian National Congress, which focused on constitutional reforms and dialogue with the British.
 
• In contrast, leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak represented the extremist faction, advocating for direct action and self-rule.

questions.question: On 25 August 2023, which State Government expanded its ongoing 'Breakfast Scheme' for students of classes 1 to 5, studying in 31,008 government schools across the State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tamil Nadu government expanded its **Breakfast Scheme** on 25 August 2023 to cover students of classes 1 to 5 in **31,008 government schools** across the state.
 
• This initiative aims to improve student attendance, reduce dropout rates, and enhance the overall nutritional status of children.
 
• The scheme provides a nutritious morning meal to children, addressing the issue of hunger and its impact on learning outcomes.
 
• Originally launched in 2022 for students of classes 1 to 5 in select schools, the program has now been scaled up to reach a significantly larger number of beneficiaries.
 
• The program has been widely praised as a pioneering step in ensuring **child welfare and education**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mid-Day Meal Scheme:**

 
 
• India’s Mid-Day Meal (MDM) Scheme was launched in 1995 to provide free lunches to schoolchildren in government schools.
 
• The scheme aims to improve **nutritional levels, school attendance, and learning outcomes** for children.
 
• It is the largest school meal program in the world.
 
• In Tamil Nadu, the MDM scheme was introduced as early as 1925, making it a pioneer in this area.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education Act (RTE):**
 
 
• The RTE Act, 2009, ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years in India.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of eliminating barriers like hunger, poverty, and lack of infrastructure in education.
 
 
 
• **Nutrition and Learning:**
 
 
• Studies show that children who receive proper nutrition perform better in academics due to improved concentration and energy levels.
 
• Programs like the Breakfast Scheme contribute significantly to addressing malnutrition and hunger among school-going children.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu’s Welfare Programs:**
 
 
• Tamil Nadu has been a frontrunner in implementing social welfare schemes, including free textbooks, uniforms, and cycles for students.
 
• The state’s focus on education and health has been instrumental in improving human development indicators.

questions.question: Which chemical compound is commonly utilised as a preservative in tomato sauce?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium Benzoate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sodium Benzoate** is a widely used chemical preservative in acidic foods, including tomato sauce, fruit juices, and pickles.
 
• It works by inhibiting the growth of bacteria, yeast, and molds, thereby prolonging shelf life.
 
• Sodium Benzoate is most effective in foods with a pH level below 4.5, making it ideal for acidic products like tomato sauce.
 
• It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) when used in prescribed limits.
 
• Sodium Benzoate is often combined with other preservatives, such as potassium sorbate, to enhance its effectiveness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mechanism of Action:** Sodium Benzoate suppresses microbial growth by creating an environment unfavorable for microbes by altering their internal pH.
 
• **Natural Occurrence:** Sodium Benzoate occurs naturally in certain fruits like cranberries, apples, and plums, though it is primarily synthesized for commercial use.
 
• **Regulations:** The permissible limit for Sodium Benzoate in food products is typically 0.1% by weight, as regulated by food safety authorities globally.
 
• **Health Considerations:** While safe in regulated amounts, excessive consumption of Sodium Benzoate may lead to allergic reactions or hyperactivity, especially when combined with artificial food dyes.
 
• **Alternative Preservatives:** Other commonly used preservatives include vinegar, citric acid, and potassium sorbate, each suitable for specific types of food products.

questions.question: The Guindy National Park is located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Guindy National Park** is located in the state of **Tamil Nadu**, India.
 
• It is situated in the capital city, **Chennai**, and is one of the smallest national parks in India, covering an area of approximately **2.70 square kilometers**.
 
• The park is home to a rich diversity of flora and fauna, including species like **spotted deer, blackbucks, and jackals**.
 
• Guindy National Park also houses a famous **Children’s Park** and a **Snake Park**, making it a popular destination for education and recreation.
 
• It is one of the few national parks located in the heart of a metropolitan city, providing a green refuge amidst urbanization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of Guindy National Park**

 
 
• The park was originally part of the grounds of the **Raj Bhavan**, the official residence of the Governor of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It was declared a reserved forest in **1910** and later designated as a national park in **1978**.
 
 
 
• **Flora in the Park**
 
 
• The park’s vegetation is predominantly **dry evergreen scrub**, a rare type of forest found in South India.
 
• It also includes grasslands and over **350 species of plants** such as shrubs, climbers, and trees.
 
 
 
• **Fauna in the Park**
 
 
• The park supports over **150 species of birds**, including parakeets, koels, and flycatchers.
 
• It is also home to reptiles like **cobras, monitor lizards, and turtles**, along with amphibians and insects.
 
 
 
• **Other Attractions**
 
 
• The **Snake Park** inside Guindy National Park showcases a variety of snakes and reptiles and is managed by the Madras Crocodile Bank Trust.
 
• The **Children’s Park** features mini-zoos and play areas, making it a family-friendly location.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts**
 
 
• The park plays a crucial role in the **conservation of endangered species** like the blackbuck.
 
• It also serves as a hub for **environmental education** and awareness programs for schools and the public.

questions.question: In which Indian state do we find caves named after elephant statues found in it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Elephanta Caves are located on **Elephanta Island** in Maharashtra, near Mumbai.
 
• The name "Elephanta" was given by Portuguese explorers due to a large stone statue of an elephant found on the island.
 
• The caves are a UNESCO **World Heritage Site** and are famous for their rock-cut sculptures dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• The most prominent feature of the caves is the **Trimurti sculpture**, depicting a three-faced depiction of Lord Shiva.
 
• The caves date back to the **5th to 8th centuries** and are a significant example of Indian rock-cut art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:**

 
 
• India has 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of 2023, including cultural, natural, and mixed sites.
 
• Examples include the Taj Mahal, Ajanta Caves, and Kaziranga National Park.
 
 
 
• **Rock-Cut Architecture:**
 
 
• It refers to structures carved directly into natural rock formations.
 
• Famous examples in India include Ajanta and Ellora Caves (Maharashtra) and Mahabalipuram (Tamil Nadu).
 
 
 
• **Elephanta Island:**
 
 
• Located in Mumbai Harbour, it is also known as **Gharapuri**, meaning "City of Caves."
 
• The island is accessible via ferry from the Gateway of India in Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Portuguese Influence:**
 
 
• The Portuguese arrived in India in the early 16th century and controlled parts of the western coast, including Mumbai.
 
• They named the island "Elephanta" after the elephant statue they found, which is now preserved in the **Jijamata Udyaan (Mumbai Zoo).**

questions.question: Which country was a major importer of dye intermediates and castor oils from India in 2022-23?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• China emerged as a major importer of dye intermediates and castor oils from India during the financial year 2022-23.
 
• Dye intermediates are chemical compounds used in the production of dyes, which are widely utilized in textiles, leather, and other industries.
 
• Castor oil is a versatile product that is heavily used in industries such as cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and lubricants.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of castor oil globally, and China is among the key markets for Indian castor oil exports.
 
• The strong trade relations between India and China make China a significant destination for various Indian chemical and agricultural exports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dye Intermediates:**

 
 
• These are precursors used in manufacturing dyes for the textile, paint, and leather industries.
 
• India is one of the leading global suppliers of dye intermediates due to its advanced chemical manufacturing capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Castor Oil:**
 
 
• Extracted from castor seeds, it is known for its high viscosity and lubricating properties.
 
• India accounts for over 90% of global castor seed production, making it the largest exporter of castor oil.
 
 
 
• **India-China Trade:**
 
 
• China is one of India's largest trading partners, with extensive imports and exports across various sectors.
 
• The trade relations encompass not only chemicals but also electronics, machinery, and other goods.
 
 
 
• **Export Dynamics:**
 
 
• India's export of dye intermediates and castor oil reflects the country's strong position in agricultural and chemical industries.
 
• These exports contribute significantly to India's foreign exchange earnings.

questions.question: The Krebs cycle of aerobic respiration is carried out within which of the following cell organelles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Krebs cycle, also known as the citric acid cycle or tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, occurs exclusively in the **mitochondria** of eukaryotic cells.
 
• This cycle is a critical part of **aerobic respiration**, where it plays a central role in energy production by oxidizing acetyl-CoA to produce ATP, NADH, and FADH₂.
 
• The mitochondria are often referred to as the **"powerhouse of the cell"** because they generate most of the cell's ATP through oxidative phosphorylation, which is closely linked to the Krebs cycle.
 
• Key enzymes involved in the Krebs cycle, such as citrate synthase and succinate dehydrogenase, are located within the **mitochondrial matrix** and inner mitochondrial membrane.
 
• The cycle is highly conserved across species, underscoring its fundamental role in cellular metabolism and energy production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondrial Matrix:**

 
 
• The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix, which contains the enzymes and substrates needed for the cycle.
 
• The matrix also houses mitochondrial DNA and ribosomes, allowing mitochondria to produce some of their own proteins.
 
 
 
• **NADH and FADH₂:**
 
 
• NADH and FADH₂ are high-energy electron carriers produced during the Krebs cycle.
 
• They donate electrons to the electron transport chain, leading to ATP synthesis via oxidative phosphorylation.
 
 
 
• **Oxidative Phosphorylation:**
 
 
• It is the process by which ATP is generated as electrons are transferred through the electron transport chain.
 
• This process is tightly coupled with the Krebs cycle, as it relies on the electron carriers (NADH and FADH₂) produced in the cycle.
 
 
 
• **Aerobic vs. Anaerobic Respiration:**
 
 
• The Krebs cycle is a feature of aerobic respiration and does not occur in anaerobic conditions.
 
• Anaerobic respiration relies on fermentation pathways, which occur in the cytoplasm and do not involve mitochondria.
 
 
 
• **Role in Biosynthesis:**
 
 
• Intermediates of the Krebs cycle, such as citrate and alpha-ketoglutarate, are precursors for biosynthetic pathways.
 
• These intermediates contribute to the synthesis of amino acids, fatty acids, and other important biomolecules.

questions.question: When the pH value of soils is more than 7.5, they are considered to be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**alkaline soils**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Soils with a pH value greater than 7.5 are classified as **alkaline soils**.
 
• Alkaline soils typically contain a high concentration of **calcium carbonate (lime)**, which raises the pH level.
 
• Such soils may exhibit poor fertility due to the reduced availability of essential nutrients like iron, manganese, and phosphorus at higher pH levels.
 
• These soils are commonly found in **arid and semi-arid regions** where evaporation exceeds precipitation, leading to salt accumulation.
 
• The correction of alkaline soils often involves adding **organic matter, sulfur compounds, or gypsum** to lower the pH and improve soil structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil pH**: A measure of the acidity or alkalinity of the soil, ranging from 0 (highly acidic) to 14 (highly alkaline), with 7 being neutral.
 
• **Acidic Soils**: Soils with a pH below 7, often found in regions with high rainfall, as leaching removes basic cations.
 
• **Neutral Soils**: Soils with a pH around 7, which are considered ideal for most agricultural crops.
 
• **Effects of High pH**: Alkaline soils can lead to deficiencies of micronutrients like zinc, iron, and copper, which are essential for plant growth.
 
• **Soil Correction**: Techniques like adding elemental sulfur, acid-forming fertilizers, or organic amendments can help lower soil pH and enhance its fertility.

questions.question: The cultural sport of Maharashtra, 'dahi-handi' is associated with which festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna Janmashtami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Dahi-handi'** is a traditional sport celebrated as part of the Krishna Janmashtami festival, marking the birth of Lord Krishna.
 
• The sport is inspired by the childhood pastime of Lord Krishna, who was fond of stealing butter from hanging pots.
 
• It involves forming human pyramids to break an earthen pot filled with curd, butter, or buttermilk, hung at a significant height.
 
• The event is celebrated with great enthusiasm, especially in Maharashtra, where it has become a cultural hallmark.
 
• The day is also marked by devotional singing, dancing, and reenactments of Lord Krishna's childhood stories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Krishna Janmashtami**: Celebrated on the eighth day (Ashtami) of the Krishna Paksha (dark fortnight) in the month of Bhadrapada as per the Hindu calendar.
 
• **Govinda Pathaks**: Teams participating in the 'dahi-handi' event are referred to as Govindas or Govinda Pathaks, named after one of Lord Krishna's titles.
 
• **Safety Measures**: In recent years, safety guidelines have been introduced to prevent injuries during the formation of human pyramids.
 
• **Regional Variations**: While Maharashtra is famous for 'dahi-handi', similar customs are observed in other states under different names and forms.
 
• **UNESCO Recognition**: Efforts have been made to include Janmashtami celebrations in UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage to highlight its cultural significance.

questions.question: Which of the following dance performances begins with the Kelikottu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kelikottu** is the traditional drum performance that marks the commencement of a Kathakali performance.
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form originating from **Kerala**, India.
 
• The art form combines elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, and facial expressions to narrate stories from epics like the **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata**.
 
• Kelikottu involves percussion instruments such as the **chenda** and **maddalam**, setting the tone for the dramatic enactment.
 
• It is performed to invite the audience and signify the beginning of the storytelling through dance and drama.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathakali** is one of the eight classical dance forms of India recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• It is known for its elaborate costumes, which include a crown (headgear), painted faces, and vibrant attire, symbolizing different characters.
 
• The stories performed in Kathakali are primarily derived from Hindu mythology, emphasizing themes of good versus evil.
 
• Performers undergo rigorous training to master the art of **mudras** (hand gestures) and facial expressions (**rasas**) to convey emotions effectively.
 
• The accompanying music and vocalists play a crucial role in enhancing the dramatic effect of the performance.

questions.question: The budget of the central government is known as the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Budget**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Union Budget** is the annual financial statement of the central government of India, as mandated by **Article 112** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It outlines the government's revenue and expenditure for the upcoming financial year, typically presented in Parliament by the **Finance Minister**.
 
• The Union Budget is presented in two parts: the **Revenue Budget** (income and expenditure) and the **Capital Budget** (capital receipts and payments).
 
• It is usually presented on **February 1st** every year to ensure the financial planning is in place before the start of the next fiscal year on April 1st.
 
• The budget serves as a comprehensive plan for economic growth, social welfare, and fiscal management by the central government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Budgets in India:**

 
 
• **Union Budget:** Presented by the central government for the entire nation.
 
• **State Budgets:** Presented by individual states for their respective jurisdictions.
 
• **Supplementary Budgets:** Presented when additional funds are required during the financial year.
 
 
 
• **Components of the Union Budget:**
 
 
• **Revenue Budget:** Includes tax and non-tax revenue and revenue expenditure.
 
• **Capital Budget:** Covers capital receipts (borrowings, disinvestment) and capital expenditure (infrastructure, investments).
 
 
 
• **Stages of Budget Presentation:**
 
 
• **Budget Speech:** Delivered by the Finance Minister in Parliament.
 
• **Budget Discussions:** Reviewed and discussed by parliamentary committees.
 
• **Approval Process:** Passed by both houses of Parliament and signed by the President.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget Significance:**
 
 
• Helps in resource allocation and planning for national priorities like healthcare, education, and defense.
 
• Acts as a tool for economic policy formulation, inflation control, and fiscal discipline.
 
• Reflects the government's vision for socio-economic development and public welfare.

questions.question: What writ means ‘We Command’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandamus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **Mandamus** originates from Latin, meaning "We Command."
 
• It is a judicial writ issued by a superior court to a lower court, tribunal, or public authority **to perform a specific duty** which is mandated by law.
 
• This writ is issued when a public official or body fails to perform their statutory duties or acts beyond their jurisdiction.
 
• Mandamus cannot be issued against private individuals or private organizations, only against public officials or institutions.
 
• This writ ensures accountability in governance and protects the rights of citizens by enforcing public duties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Habeas Corpus**:

 
 
• Latin for "You may have the body," this writ is used to ensure that a person is not detained unlawfully.
 
• It protects an individual’s right to liberty by directing authorities to produce the detained person in court.
 
 
 
• **Certiorari**:
 
 
• Derived from Latin meaning "To be informed," this writ is issued by a higher court to review the decision of a lower court or tribunal.
 
• It ensures that the lower court’s decision does not exceed its jurisdiction or violate procedural law.
 
 
 
• **Prohibition**:
 
 
• A writ issued by a superior court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• It is a preventive measure ensuring that judicial or quasi-judicial bodies operate within their legal limits.
 
 
 
• **Quo Warranto**:
 
 
• Latin for "By what authority," this writ challenges a person’s right to hold a public office.
 
• It ensures that public offices are not usurped unlawfully or without legal authority.
